bull.b: Rapid TTM revenue growth alongside a shift to positive gross margin indicates improving commercial traction and product economics. If maintained, the stronger revenue base can provide operating leverage and create a more credible path toward covering fixed costs and reducing losses.

Exchanging unsecured notes into preferred equity removes a material debt obligation, while repayment of the Wattbike facility reduces financing-related commitments. This reshapes the capital structure and may improve financial flexibility, although the preferred stock remains senior to common equity.

The planned STEPR acquisition could materially expand the revenue base and extend the company’s connected fitness platform beyond its existing operations. Management also expects the combined business to reach positive Adjusted EBITDA, creating a potential route toward better operating scale.

bear.b: Losses remain far too large relative to the current revenue base, showing that the company has not yet developed a sustainable cost structure. Even with stronger sales and gross margin, continued operating deficits could delay profitability and require further financing.

Negative operating and free cash flow means the business is not currently funding itself through operations. Persistent cash consumption increases reliance on external capital, limits flexibility to invest in growth, and raises financing risk if losses continue.

High leverage leaves the capital base vulnerable because debt remains large relative to equity and returns on equity are strongly negative. Authorized conversions, new preferred securities, and equity issuance can further dilute common holders while senior claims remain ahead of them.
